back_translation: Oh how the gold has grown dim, the fine pure gold turned dull! The sacred gems lie scattered at every street corner.
The precious sons of Zion, once worth their weight in finest gold — oh how they are now reckoned as mere clay pots, the work of a potter's hands!
Even jackals offer the breast to suckle their young, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
The nursing infant's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst. Little children ask for food, but no one offers them any.
Those who once ate delicacies are destitute in the streets; those brought up in deep scarlet embrace ash heaps instead.
The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than the penalty of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant with no hand turned to help her.
Her nobles were once purer and brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their complexion more ruddy than coral, their form like sapphire.
But now their faces are blacker than soot; they go unrecognized in the streets. Their skin clings shriveled to their bones, dry as a stick of wood.
Those slain by the sword are better off than those slain by hunger, who waste away, pierced through, for lack of the produce of the field.
The hands of once-compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became food for them in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
The LORD has vented His wrath to the full; He has poured out His fierce anger. He kindled a fire in Zion, and it devoured her foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe — nor did any inhabitants of the world — that adversary or enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
But it was because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in her midst.
They staggered like the blind through the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one dared touch their garments.
People cried at them, 'Go away! Unclean! Away, away! Do not touch!' So they fled and wandered, and among the nations it was said, 'They can dwell here no longer.'
The face of the LORD has scattered them; they will receive no more regard. The priests are shown no honor; the elders receive no mercy.
Our eyes grew weary looking in vain for our help. We watched and watched from our towers for a nation that could not save.
They tracked our every step so that we could not walk in our squares. Our end drew near; our days were fulfilled, for our end had come.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky; they chased us over the mountains and lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
The one anointed by the LORD, who was the very life-breath to us, was caught in their pits — he of whom we had said, 'Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.'
Rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom, dweller in the land of Uz! But the cup will come around to you as well; you will become drunk and strip yourself naked.
O Daughter of Zion, the punishment of your iniquity is complete; He will not send you into exile again. But O Daughter of Edom, He will punish your iniquity; He will lay bare your sins.
